refined_question:
Determine the exact value of the constant c for the unit interval [0,1] with Lebesgue measure and central symmetries, where
ms([0,1], r) := inf_{[0,1]=A1∪⋯∪Ar} max_{1≤i≤r} sup{ λ(B) : B ⊆ Ai is measurable and B = x - B for some x ∈ R },
the infimum being taken over all measurable r-colorings (partitions) of [0,1]. Equivalently, compute the asymptotic constant
c = lim_{r→∞} ms([0,1], r) r^2 = inf_{r≥2} ms([0,1], r) r^2,
known from the paper’s cited source to satisfy 1/2 ≤ c ≤ 5/6.
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the paper’s explicit open problem in Section 8 rather than a neighboring topic: Problem 8.4 asks to calculate the constant from Theorem 8.1(7). The surrounding Section 8 text introduces the interval invariant ms([0,1], r), explains that it concerns measurable colorings of the unit interval and monochromatic symmetric subsets, and situates Theorem 8.1 as the summary of the interval results. The precise asymptotic content behind Theorem 8.1(7) is the original theorem proved in the cited source [7, §6]: Theorem 6.8(2) states that ms([0,1], r) = c r^-2 (1 + o(1)) for some constant c with 1/2 ≤ c ≤ 5/6, and the proof identifies c as the limit of ms([0,1], r) r^2; together with Theorem 6.1(2)-(3) and Lemma 6.7, this yields the common limit/infimum formulation. So the paper-faithful stand-alone question is exactly to compute that constant for measurable r-colorings of [0,1] under central symmetry.
